title: Amazon Bedrock vs Amazon SageMaker AI
summary: Bedrock provides serverless API access to leading foundation models (Anthropic Claude, Amazon Titan, Meta Llama, Cohere, AI21) with built-in Knowledge Bases (RAG), Agents, and Guardrails without managing infrastructure. SageMaker AI is a complete end-to-end ML platform for building, training, tuning, and deploying custom models, containers, and pipelines.
keyTakeaway: Use Bedrock for fast, serverless GenAI integration and managed RAG; use SageMaker for custom model architectures, specialized container training, and ML lifecycle engineering.
examTip: Exam questions asking for "minimal operational overhead" or "serverless API to foundation models" point to Amazon Bedrock.

title: Bedrock Knowledge Bases & Vector Databases
summary: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases automates end-to-end RAG workflows: parsing documents in Amazon S3, generating embeddings via Titan Embeddings, storing vectors in Amazon OpenSearch Serverless, Pinecone, or Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL (pgvector), and executing semantic retrieval.
keyTakeaway: Knowledge Bases handles chunking, vectorization, synchronization, and context retrieval fully managed.
examTip: Look for OpenSearch Serverless as the default native vector storage option in Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases.

title: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails & Responsible AI
summary: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails enforces safety, privacy, and compliance across any foundation model on Bedrock or custom models. It supports content filtering (hate, insults, violence), denied topics, PII redaction/blocking, word filters, and automated Contextual Grounding checks to prevent hallucinations.
keyTakeaway: Contextual Grounding score evaluates how factually grounded the model output is against the reference source documents.
examTip: To detect and mitigate hallucinations and prevent PII leakage across foundation models, configure Bedrock Guardrails.

title: Fine-Tuning vs RAG vs Prompt Engineering
summary: Prompt Engineering requires zero training and modifies prompts at inference. RAG injects dynamic external data into prompts without retraining weights. Fine-tuning adjusts model weights using domain-specific labeled dataset pairs for consistent tone or proprietary syntax.
keyTakeaway: RAG is optimal for fresh knowledge and preventing hallucination; Fine-Tuning is optimal for specialized formats, styles, or domain terminology where knowledge retrieval alone is insufficient.
examTip: If the business requirement is access to real-time internal corporate documents, choose RAG. If requirement is domain tone/grammar, choose Fine-tuning.

title: AWS Responsible AI Principles & Bias Detection
summary: AWS adheres to 6 Responsible AI pillars: Fairness, Explainability, Robustness, Privacy & Security, Governance, and Transparency. SageMaker Clarify detects bias across pre-training and post-training data and provides model explainability (SHAP values). SageMaker Model Cards document model purpose and performance metrics.
keyTakeaway: Use SageMaker Clarify for bias detection & explainability; SageMaker Model Cards for governance and audit documentation.
examTip: When asked how to audit and document a model for regulatory and compliance review, use SageMaker Model Cards.
